title: Outsource or keep in-house?: a quick guide for case interviews
description: Make-or-buy questions in operations and cost cases.
hook: Make-or-buy questions come up in operations and cost cases: should the client keep something in-house or hand it to someone else? Here are the trade-offs in one place.
body:
When it helps

Make-or-buy questions in operations and cost cases.

The comparison

ForAgainst
OutsourceLower cost; focus on the core; less risk if volumes fallLess control over quality; reliance on others; brand risk
Keep in-houseControl over process and quality; keeps know-howHigher fixed costs; capacity tied up

An example

A bank is thinking of outsourcing its customer call centre. For: lower cost per call and easier to scale up and down. Against: customers may notice a worse service, and the bank loses direct contact with what customers are complaining about. A sensible middle way is often to outsource simple calls and keep complex or high-value ones in-house.

How it sounds in an interview

I'd weigh what we gain, mostly cost and flexibility, against what we risk: quality, control and know-how. A split approach is often possible.

Use it lightly

Treat this as a prompt for your own thinking, not a script. Pick the parts that matter for this client, say why, and leave the rest out. A short, relevant list beats a complete one every time.
outro: Small things like this add up. Try it in your next practice case and notice how it changes the conversation. All of these sit on the free frameworks page, next to the 11 core trees.
